prompts.title: Loose watercolor painting of anything
prompts.tool: Any image AI (ChatGPT / Gemini / Midjourney / Grok)
prompts.prompt: Abstract watercolor wash of a [subject], loose oversized brushstrokes, broad flowing color shapes, minimal detail, soft pigment bleeding, expressive wet-on-wet texture, simplified forms, airy composition, no linework, no outlines, white background
prompts.why: Swap [subject] for a pet, city or object. 'No linework, no outlines' is what stops the AI from drawing a cartoon and keeps it looking like real wet paint.
prompts.author: @azed_ai

prompts.title: Paper cut-out storybook character
prompts.tool: Any image AI (ChatGPT / Gemini / Midjourney / Grok)
prompts.prompt: Paper cut-out animation of a [subject] [simple action], full-body character, layered paper shapes, handmade paper texture, visible cut edges, soft shadows between layers, flat colorful paper tones, slightly imperfect handcrafted details, minimal paper-collage scenery, charming folk story aesthetic, gentle stop-motion feel, poetic children’s book atmosphere, clean white background
prompts.why: Fill in two blanks, e.g. 'a fox' + 'reading a book'. 'Visible cut edges' and 'soft shadows between layers' sell the handmade paper look.
prompts.author: @azed_ai

prompts.title: Cinematic 3D fantasy character
prompts.tool: Any image AI (ChatGPT / Gemini / Midjourney / Grok)
prompts.prompt: A cinematic 3D full-body render of [fantasy character], wearing [armor design] assembled from salvaged robotic parts, [facial features], [hairstyle], carrying [weapon], distressed fabrics, corroded metal plating, exposed mechanisms, intricate mechanical details, battle-worn appearance, realistic PBR textures, stylized realism, dramatic studio lighting, Unreal Engine 5 quality, clean white background
prompts.why: Fill the five blanks (e.g. an elf knight, a samurai helmet, a long bow). The material words like corroded metal and PBR textures are what make it look like a game render instead of a cartoon.

prompts.title: 60-second animated explainer in one HTML file
prompts.prompt:
<context>I want a 60-second animated explainer about [TOPIC] to post on X and LinkedIn. I have no editing software and no animation skills.</context>
<task>Write a short script and shot list first: 8 to 12 shots, with what's on screen, the on-screen text and the timing for each. Then build the whole video as one HTML file with three.js, with every shot animated, smooth transitions and background music and sound effects made with the Web Audio API.</task>
<rules>Keep on-screen text to 8 words or fewer per shot so it reads on a phone. Use one colour palette and one font throughout so it looks like a brand film. Make it 1080x1080 so it fits every feed.</rules>
<output>One HTML file that plays the full video when opened, with a Record button that saves it as a video file I can upload.</output>
<input>[TOPIC]</input>
prompts.why: Swap [TOPIC] for your product or idea. Paste into Claude Opus 5.5 — you get a playable HTML explainer with no editing apps.

prompts.title: Attention audit for your posts and offers
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a growth auditor who has watched talented people with great products earn nothing because nobody saw them. You judge a business by who knows about it, not by how good it is. You also know an AI's default is to polish the product and ignore distribution, which is how good work stays invisible.

Your mission: find out how much attention my work actually captures today and where it leaks. Koe writes: "Getting a million views on one tweet or reel is useless if the rest of your posts get a thousand views a pop." Before any output, think step by step: who sees my work, how often, and what they do next.

---

PHASE 1: The Evidence

Give me three things:

What you sell or want to sell, in one sentence.
Your last 20 posts with their views.
Where your last 5 customers or opportunities came from.

→ Type "continue"

PHASE 2: The Reach Gap

The difference between my best post and my typical post, and what that says about my brand versus my content.

→ Type "continue"

PHASE 3: The Leaks

Where attention arrives and dies: no follow-up, no offer, no reason to come back. I name each leak.

→ Type "continue"

PHASE 4: The Fix

The one change to my posting this month that turns one-off views into people who come back.

→ Type "complete" for your attention audit.
prompts.why: Paste real post stats when it asks. Type continue between phases. Ends with one concrete posting fix instead of a vague growth pep talk.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter

prompts.title: Brand interview that builds your intellectual signature
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a brand strategist who refuses to write a word for a client until the onboarding interview is done. You've seen hundreds of founders post generic content because nobody ever asked them the right questions. You also know an AI's default is to invent a brand from a job title, which is how everyone ends up sounding the same.

Your mission: interview me and build the brand document every future draft will start from. Koe writes: "Almost nobody accounts for brand strategy." Before any output, think step by step: who I help, what I've lived through, what I believe that others don't.

---

PHASE 1: The Reader

Give me three things:

One real person you want to help, described in detail.
What they say when they complain to a friend, in their words.
What they've already tried that didn't work.

→ Type "continue"

PHASE 2: The Story

Ask me, one question at a time, about the moment things changed for me and what I've built, tried and failed at.

→ Type "continue"

PHASE 3: The Beliefs

What I believe that most people in my space don't, the advice I think is wrong, and the way of living I want to help people escape.

→ Type "continue"

PHASE 4: The Document

My full brand document on one page, using only my answers.

→ Type "complete" for your brand document.
prompts.why: Answer honestly through the four phases. You get a one-page brand doc from your words — reuse it before every draft so the AI stops inventing a generic founder voice.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
